signal: Prove launched its Identity Platform as a trust layer for an agentic world and raised $40M from MassMutual and Capital One Ventures

email.body1:
Andrew, saw Prove launched its Identity Platform as a trust layer for an agentic world off the new $40M round.

A launch that size usually pulls in more in-market accounts than the team can touch, and the gap between a signal landing and a rep acting on it quietly costs pipeline. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for Prove off your hiring and tech-stack data, and accounts showing those signals tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Andrew, quick follow-up for Prove.

Most RevOps leaders know exactly where the data is messy but never get time to fix the signal-to-action handoff. That is usually where the measurable lift hides, and a few sequencing changes often move reply rates more than a new tool does.

Worth 15 minutes? I will walk you through a teardown of your current outbound and 3 things I would change. Our best practices alone usually lift response rates 50 to 70 percent.
email.body3:
Andrew, last bit of proof for Prove.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Prove's reply rate likely compares to peer B2B software teams. Want to grab a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Andrew, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If tightening signal-to-action latency is not a RevOps priority this quarter, no problem at all. I know post-launch quarters get loud, and not every initiative makes the cut.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of 3 AI-SDR plays scoped to your motion? I will tailor it to Prove either way.
